title: Move the 16 not-attempted client-test stubs onto the shared fake (LIN-4255 leftovers)
description:
Follow-up to LIN-4252 and LIN-4255. **Rewritten in the LIN-4255 close-out** (the earlier text described LIN-4252's 18 `makeContainer` files; LIN-4255 has since moved most of them onto the shared fake).

## Problem

16 test files still hand-write a single-element stub for a `public/` client script. They are on `HAND_WRITTEN_FAKE_DOM_FILES` in `tests/unit/fake-dom-census.test.js`, so the census ratchet keeps them listed and nothing can add to the list. None was attempted by LIN-4255: no move piece of its approved plan covered them (LIN-4255 plan-review note 1b), so they were dropped from that ticket and routed here. They are not stopped. Each is a single-element stub that the shared fake (`tests/unit/helpers/fake-dom.js`, with `tests/unit/helpers/client-world.js` `loadWorld` over it) can serve as it stands.

## The 16 files (all under `tests/unit/`)

Pre-move checks first (verify once when the file is moved):

* `run-limit-gating.test.js`: `querySelector` returns null (line 121). Its moved path reaches the `querySelector ?` guards in LIN-4292.
* `runner-link-surfaces.test.js`: same stub (line 169). `style` is written only on the animation path (`public/swipe.js:534-551`), which this suite does not reach. Verify once.
* `lin-4024-home-description.test.js`: `public/app.js:169` and `:427` write `style.display`. Confirm they are off the description path.
* `lin-3975-proposal-refresh.test.js`: confirm the `idInput` / `questionInput` hooks are `<input>` / `<textarea>` (`public/task-chat.js:35-36`).

Others (12), feasible with the modelled APIs:

* `close-out-client.test.js`
* `dashboard-routes.test.js`
* `lin-2122-history-outcome-pill.test.js`
* `lin-2370-browser-copy-prompt-provider-identity.test.js`
* `lin-3254-session-run-toggles.test.js`
* `lin-4016-sessions-fold-parked.test.js`
* `lin-4024-look.test.js`
* `lin-4242-waiting-live.test.js`
* `question-card-task-bound.test.js`
* `task-page-client.test.js`
* `task-page-link-client-surfaces.test.js`
* `task-page-question.test.js`

## Not in this ticket

The 9 census entries stopped on an API the fake does not model (`style` / `getBoundingClientRect`, `<select>.value`, real bubbling `dispatchEvent`) stay on the list with their stop reason in the census comments. Removing the `querySelector` guards in `public/` is LIN-4292.

## Acceptance

* Each moved file leaves `HAND_WRITTEN_FAKE_DOM_FILES` in the same change and joins the `fake-dom.js` header's consumer list.
* Each moved suite keeps its test names and counts (diff sorted test names on base and branch). A test that goes red on the real DOM is reported as a finding, not loosened.
* A file that turns out to need a stop API stays on the list with a comment naming the API and `file:line`.
* `fake-dom-census.test.js` and `claude-md-line-budget.test.js` stay green; the count on the list only falls.

## Method

One family per PR, by the grouping above, as LIN-4255 did: assertion map, before/after test names, a mutation showing each load-bearing assertion goes red.

*Note (20:55, from LIN-4304): when* `close-out-client.test.js` *moves, remove the* `typeof … === 'function'` *seams in* `public/close-out.js` *(around 159/161/175) and their entries in LIN-4304's allow-list.*

## At merge (each piece)

* The census falls by the number moved, and each remaining entry's reason is true now.
* The derived consumer list is green.
* Every red-then-classified test is listed.
* The full unit suite passes.

## Implementation Plan

*Pruned in the LIN-4254 close-out; the full pre-prune description is preserved in the task snapshots, and the plan, its revisions and the scoping call are in the comment trail.*

**Implemented as approved.** The plan needed multiple sessions (needs multiple sessions: Piece 0 plus groups 1-5, sequential because each edits the census list) and was built as seven sub-tickets, each its own PR:

* LIN-4306 piece 0, probe + computed consumer list: PR #2321 (`165c61e7`)
* LIN-4307 piece 1: PR #2322 (`f73f1b11`)
* LIN-4308 piece 2: `3f4d4131`
* LIN-4309 piece 3: PR #2327 (`8b84a8fe`)
* LIN-4310 piece 4: `ff6a69fa`
* LIN-4311 piece 5: `90542b2c`
* LIN-4312 piece 6: PR #2331 (`ce42e721`)
* Close-out anchor fix: PR #2335 (`afe9074f`)

Result: census 22 -> 6 (the six original stop cases), all 16 files on `loadWorld`, test names preserved (573 -> 579, no losses), `close-out.js` typeof seams removed. Deviations: the loader now makes `window` the global (pinned in `client-world.test.js`), and `dashboard-routes`' badge test moved to `rulings-badge-client.test.js`.

### Session fit and review (kept verbatim; code reads these lines)

needs multiple sessions — six PRs (Piece 0 plus groups 1–5), sequential because each edits the census list, each verified on its own, and the last gated on LIN-4304. Build it as sequential dispatches or sub-tickets in that order.

comments.body: Priority: lowest. Test-only tidy with no production effect and no recurring risk; its value is making LIN-4246-style repaint witnesses cheap in each file as it is touched. Type label: Improvement (nearest in the catalog; no test-infra label exists). LIN-4252 merged as d234b94a; the shared fake now models `type` and `checked` too.

Rewritten in the LIN-4255 close-out (review comment cb4cbff9, ledger item 1): the description now lists exactly the 16 census entries LIN-4255 never attempted, with the 4 pre-move checks, instead of LIN-4252 18 makeContainer files (most already moved). Priority unchanged (Low).

## Survey global: LIN-4254 @ b581ac926

**Where it lands.** `tests/unit/`: 16 client suites, `fake-dom-census.test.js` (22 entries at base, 6 with stop comments, 16 without), and the header of `helpers/fake-dom.js`. It is improving fast: the census went from 56 to 22 over 13 PRs on 2026-11-05, against a list enforced both ways. Meanwhile `fake-dom.js` reached 1054 lines, and its header's consumer list is a ~25-line paragraph nothing checks; the census only *tells* you to update it (census :648-649).

**What the obvious move does.** Each file is really two moves, not one. None of the 16 uses `loadWorld`: each builds its own `vm.createContext` sandbox (2–7 vm calls per file). So the task also retires 16 private copies of `client-world.js`; wrapping each sandbox around the fake instead would keep a second loader in every file. Three suites load a *slice* of a script rather than the whole file: `lin-2122` and `lin-3254` slice by `indexOf`, and `dashboard-routes` slices `updateRulingsBadge` at :6860. `loadWorld({ scripts: [] })` + `world.run` already covers this (precedent: `task-chat-flight-companion-sentinel-mask`, LIN-4284).

"Single-element stub" understates some of these:
- `question-card-task-bound` builds a whole card by regex over the rendered markup, with a `querySelector` switch and a hand-rolled `click()` (:46-97). The fake has no `click()`, so this one needs `clickOn`.
- `querySelector: () => null` appears in at least six files, not just the two the ticket flags. On a real tree those lookups *succeed*, so code paths that were dead in these tests come alive. Expect red tests that are findings.
- `dashboard-routes` is a 6910-line server-route suite with 257 tests. Its only fake is in one test that pipes a handler's JSON into a client slice. Moved in place, it becomes the only server suite importing `client-world.js`.
- `question-card-task-bound`, `task-page-question` and `lin-4242-waiting-live` load `question-cards.js`, whose bubbling `dispatchEvent` (:235-244) stopped three other suites. They miss it only because no `CustomEvent` is in the sandbox (`typeof CustomEvent` guard). Keep it that way, or they reach the stop.

**Who has to learn about it.** The census list is enforced. The header consumer list is not, and will drift silently by 16 names. CLAUDE.md needs no change. `public/close-out.js` has 4 `typeof … === 'function'` seams, and `common.js` and `prompt-section.js` have one each. Those exist *because* the stubs were partial.

**Better, at a cost this task can carry.**
1. Have the census compute the actual importers of `fake-dom.js`/`client-world.js` and assert that the header names each one.
2. Delete each file's private sandbox outright rather than adapting it, so "moved" means "on `loadWorld`", not just "uses `createFakeDom`".

**Better still, not this task's.** The ticket is aimed at a number; the deeper symptom is that `public/` carries seams shaped around test stubs (the `typeof` guards, the `querySelector ?` guards in LIN-4292, the `typeof CustomEvent` early-return). This task is the precondition for removing them, so LIN-4292/LIN-4304 should follow family by family rather than wait for all 16. Separately, whether `fake-dom.js` should model bubbling `dispatchEvent` decides the last 3 stopped suites; that decision is bigger than this ticket.

## Survey open-0: LIN-4254 @ b581ac926

Read in a worktree at `b581ac926`. The 16 suites plus the census pass at base (571/571).

**The premise is the hard part.** The ticket says each file is "a single-element stub the shared fake can serve as it stands." A scratch run of the census with an empty list shows 5 files hold more than one shape: `task-page-client` 7, `close-out-client` 3, and `lin-4242-waiting-live`, `task-page-link-client-surfaces` and `task-page-question` 2 each. Most shapes are not elements. There are three kinds:

1. **Argument seams**, where a pure function is handed an object (`close-out-client`'s boxes, `task-page-client:415`). These are cheap to convert with `createFakeDom` + `parse`.
2. **Document routers**, where `querySelector(sel)` maps to hand-made objects (`task-page-client:328/399`, `task-page-question:221-253`, `lin-3975:157`). The real fake returns null unless the markup exists, so each move means writing page markup. That is fixture authoring, not a swap.
3. **Auto-vivifiers**, where every selector returns an element: `el(sel)` in `runner-link-surfaces:184` and `task-page-link-client-surfaces:47`, and a `Proxy` over the whole document and window in `lin-4024-home-description:70`. They run whole page inits (`app.js`, `swipe.js` + `common.js`) where every write is a no-op. On the fake those paths go live, and that is where stop APIs will surface, not where the pre-checks look:
   - `task-page-link-client-surfaces` loads `swipe.js` (26 `style`/layout hits) and stubs `style: {}`, yet sits in the "feasible" 12.
   - `app.js:1679` uses `insertAdjacentHTML('afterend')`, which the fake throws on.

`question-card-task-bound` asserts through stub `.click()` and `card.removed`, so its assertion map changes (to `clickOn`/`isConnected`). Its card matches the `dispatchEvent`-stopped shape. It is safe only because `announceRulingGone` (`question-cards.js:236`) exits without `CustomEvent`, which `loadWorld` doesn't supply.

**Stale wording.**
- LIN-4292 already landed (`b389f9b0`, before base: "unblocks no test suite"), so the `run-limit-gating` pre-check is moot.
- The census lists 6 stops, not 9.
- LIN-4304's allow-list isn't on main. Removing the `typeof` seams at `close-out.js:158-159,174` is a production change, and it collides with "keep test names and counts": `close-out-client:242` exists to feed those seams hand-made docs. Do that removal after LIN-4304 lands, as its own step.

**Grouping.** "Family by the grouping above" yields 4 pre-checks and 12 others, not families. Group by client script:
- task-page (`task-page-client`, `task-page-question`, `lin-3975`, `close-out-client`)
- question-cards
- `common.js` slices (`dashboard-routes`, which is one test at :6878 in a 6,910-line suite, `lin-4242-waiting-live`, `lin-2370`)
- sessions/app (`lin-3254`, `lin-4016`, both `lin-4024`)
- swipe/prompt-section (`runner-link`, `task-page-link`, `run-limit-gating`, `lin-2122`)

**First:**
1. Tag every flagged shape as seam, router or auto-vivifier.
2. Probe the three auto-vivifiers on `loadWorld` with an empty body and see what throws. They are the likeliest to stay on the list, and knowing early resizes the ticket.
3. Decide where router markup comes from. Prefer the server's real renderer over hand-written HTML, or the fixture drifts the way the stub did.

### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict:** Request Changes. The plan is sound and its facts hold at HEAD. One step has no workable path: Piece 2's `dashboard-routes` move. The obvious ways to build it either copy a fixture or drop the server half of the witness.

Blocking findings: 1

Reviewed at `b581ac92` (= origin/main; nothing under `tests/` or `public/` has landed since the plan was written).

**What I checked, and it holds:**
- The census has 22 entries: 6 carry a `// stop:` comment and the other 16 are exactly this ticket's files.
- None of the 16 uses `loadWorld`, and each builds its own `vm` context.
- On main, the 16 files plus `fake-dom-census` and `claude-md-line-budget` pass 573/573. The plan's 571 left out the budget test.
- These line references are correct: `app.js:1679` (`afterend`), `app.js:169/427` (`style.display`), `question-cards.js:236` (the `CustomEvent` guard), `close-out.js:158-161/174-175/187` and `task-chat.js:33-37`.
- None of the three question-card suites supplies `CustomEvent` today, so moving them to `loadWorld` keeps the event path off as it is now.
- LIN-4304 is In Progress, not merged. Gating Piece 5 on it is right.

### Blocking

**1. Piece 2: the `dashboard-routes` client test has no fixture to move with.** The test at `tests/unit/dashboard-routes.test.js:6858` runs the real `/workspace/:urlKey/api/dashboard/rulings` handler and feeds its JSON to the sliced `updateRulingsBadge`. That cross-seam is the whole witness: a badge that reads `count` instead of `workspaceCount` paints 3, not 1.

The server half comes from about 270 lines that exist only inside that file: `makeStores` (:55), `findRouteLayer`/`getHandler` (:110/:127), `makeReqRes` (:132), `makeRouter` (:148), `decisionItem` (:325), plus the `withDefaults` wrapper (:32). A client suite cannot import them, because importing a test file re-runs its 257 tests (the census header says why at :22-24). So the plan as written leaves the builder three ways forward, and two are ruled out:
- copy the fixture into the client suite. The ticket rules this out by name: "LIN-4296's `lin-4296-scope-pick` copied its parent's fixture".
- replace the route with a canned `{ count, workspaceCount }`. That breaks "fixtures come from the server's real code, not hand-written", and a later rename of `workspaceCount` would no longer turn it red.
- extract the fixture. This is a refactor the plan does not sequence.

**Change:** make Piece 2's first commit a pure extraction. Move those helpers into one shared module (for example `tests/fixtures/dashboard-router.js`). `dashboard-routes` imports it, its sorted test names are unchanged, and it never imports `client-world.js`. Then the badge test moves to a named client suite that imports that module plus `loadWorld({ scripts: [] })` and `world.run(slice)`. No client unit suite covers `updateRulingsBadge` today; the e2e specs do. So either name the existing suite it joins or say a new one is created, and include it in the name map.

### Notes for the builder (not blocking)

**2. Piece 0's empty-body probe throws on setup gaps, not on missing APIs.** I ran it in scratch on `loadWorld` with an empty body:
- `scripts: ['app.js']` throws `TypeError: window.addEventListener is not a function`.
- `scripts: ['common.js', 'swipe.js']` throws at load: `swipe.js:84` queries `.swipe-filter-select` at top level and `:943` calls `addEventListener` on the null result.

Neither is an API the fake does not model, so neither may become a census stop reason. The predicted stops sit behind real markup: `app.js:1679` only runs on a `.dispatch-disclosure-placeholder`. Probe with the window stubs the suite already passes and the renderer's markup. Record as a stop only a `FakeDomError`, a `style`/layout read, or a call to an unmodelled method. Other unmodelled methods on these paths: `click()`, at `app.js:71`, `app.js:2010` and `prompt-section.js:2612`; the fake deliberately has no `click`.

**3. Scripts that query the DOM at load need their markup in place first.** `loadWorld` has no `markup` option; that is LIN-4289/LIN-4297 item 1 and is not on main. Suites loading `swipe.js` (`runner-link-surfaces`, `task-page-link-client-surfaces`) must call `loadWorld({ scripts: [] })`, `parse(markup, document.body)`, then `world.run(source)`, as `observation-ruling-delivery` does. That is still "on `loadWorld`", not a wrapped sandbox. Say so in Piece 4.

**4. Piece 0's derived consumer list, as specified, starts red on main and keeps the hand step.**
- The header already misses `lin-4293-tidy-after-repaint.test.js`, which imports `client-world.js` directly (`:18`). Add it in Piece 0.
- Parse only the consumer sentences. The header also names `fake-dom-census.test.js` as the guard, and that file imports nothing, so a "named but no importer" rule run over the whole header goes red on it. `helpers/client-world.js` and `helpers/live-console-world.js` are real importers and stay in the list.
- The plan says this "replaces the hand step". It doesn't: every move still edits the header, and the census now enforces that. The census stale-file message (:648-649) should keep telling people to edit it.
- LIN-4297's Done-when says "No hand-kept consumer list remains". When this item leaves LIN-4297, the note there must also change that line. Otherwise LIN-4297 deletes what Piece 0 builds.
- Better: if the header could say "the consumers are the importers the census computes" and drop the names, the 16 moves wouldn't touch it at all, and LIN-4297 item 4 would be done. Your scope call reads both ways ("the header names every real importer" vs "so the moves don't hand-edit that list 16 times"). I'd take the second, but the plan's reading is defensible, so this is not blocking.

**5. Piece 5 seams.** `close-out.js:187` (`typeof box.appendChild !== 'function'`) is the same unit seam as `:159/:161/:175`, but `appendChild` is outside LIN-4304's method list, so it will have no allow-list entry. Decide it in the same production commit; I recommend removing it, since `close-out-client`'s boxes become real elements.

**6. The early close-out needs a ticket, not a relation.** If LIN-4304 hasn't merged and this ticket closes with `close-out-client` left over, a `blocked-by` on a closed LIN-4254 hides that leftover. File a follow-up for the `close-out-client` move plus the seam removal, marked blocked-by LIN-4304. "Relations to record" should say the same: a step can't carry a relation.

**7. Grouping is loose but harmless.** `lin-3254` loads `session.js`, not sessions/app. `lin-2122` slices `dispatch.js`, and `run-limit-gating` loads `prompt-section.js`, not `swipe.js`. The order only matters for census conflicts, so keep it.

### Plan revised in the description (answers the Plan Review Verdict)

All seven findings are answered; I disagreed with none. Facts re-checked at `b581ac92`.

1. **Blocking, `dashboard-routes` fixture:** Piece 2 now opens with a pure extraction of the route fixture (`makeStores`, `findRouteLayer`/`getHandler`, `makeReqRes`, `makeRouter`, `decisionItem`, `withDefaults`) into a shared module. `dashboard-routes` imports it back with identical sorted names and count. The badge test then moves to a new client suite, since no unit suite covers `updateRulingsBadge`. The rename mutation shows why a canned payload would not do.
2. **Probe:** it now runs with each suite's window stubs and the renderer's markup. Only a `FakeDomError`, a `style` or layout read, or an unmodelled method (`click()` included) counts as a stop reason.
3. **No `markup` option:** swipe-loading suites use `scripts: []`, `parse`, then `world.run`.
4. **Consumer list:** I took the review's preferred reading. The header stops naming consumers and the census computes them, so the 16 moves never edit it. `lin-4293` is covered by the scan. The LIN-4297 Done-when line is noted to be met by Piece 0.
5. **`close-out.js:187`:** removed in the same production commit as the other seams.
6. **Early close:** a follow-up ticket blocked-by LIN-4304 is filed at that point. No relation goes on a closed LIN-4254.
7. **Grouping labels:** corrected; order kept.

Session fit: needs multiple sessions. plan-review due: yes.

### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict:** Approve. Every point in the 20:39 verdict is answered and each answer holds at HEAD. The new Piece 2 extraction is buildable as written. What's left are notes for the builder.

Reviewed at `b581ac92` (= origin/main; still nothing new under `tests/` or `public/`). LIN-4304 is still In Progress, so the Piece 5 gate stands.

**Previous findings, re-checked:**
1. **`dashboard-routes` fixture (was blocking): resolved.** `makeStores` (:55), `findRouteLayer`/`getHandler` (:110/:127), `makeReqRes` (:132), `makeRouter` (:148) and `decisionItem` (:325) are plain functions. None uses a `before()` hook, a mutable module variable or a `test()` call. A no-test module can hold them, and importing it runs nothing. Each one is also used by other tests, so the "only multi-use helpers move" rule takes exactly this set. The badge test (:6858) is the file's only fake. Once it moves, the census entry goes and the file has no `vm` use left.
2. **Probe with real stubs and markup, and the stop-reason rule: holds.**
3. **`scripts: []` + `parse` + `world.run` for top-level-querying scripts: holds.** `loadWorld` has no `markup` option on main.
4. **Consumer list: holds in direction.** It matches LIN-4297 item 4's own wording ("derive the consumer list from the census, and delete the hand-kept copy"). Both places that tell people to hand-edit the list are named: the census stale message (:648-649) and the header (`fake-dom.js:32`). CLAUDE.md doesn't mention the list. See note A on how narrow the new check must be.
5. **`close-out.js:187`: holds.** The four seams are at :159, :161, :175 and :187 at HEAD.
6. **Follow-up ticket instead of a relation: holds.**
7. **Grouping: holds.**

### Notes for the builder (none blocking)

**A. Piece 0: aim the "header names a consumer" check at the paragraph, not the whole header.** The plan's rule is "fails if the header again hand-lists a consumer file name". Run over the whole header, it goes red on main on names that aren't the list:
- `fake-dom.js:5` names `fake-dom.test.js`, a real importer, as the fake's own tests.
- `:9` and `:13` name `client-world.js`.

The plan exempts `client-world.js` and `live-console-world.js` but not `fake-dom.test.js`. Two ways to fix it, smallest first:
- check only the "Guard and consumers" paragraph, or
- allow exactly those three helper and own-test names.

The plan's "real run green on main" witness would catch this, so it is a note. Also, the computed importer set has no reader except this check. If the header's pointer says "the importers the census computes", make the census message print that set when the check fails, so a reader can find it. (The census file names `fake-dom.js` only as a string in `EXCLUDED`, so an AST `ImportDeclaration` scan correctly leaves it out. A text grep would not.)

**B. Piece 2 extraction: `decisionItem` reads the module constant `NOW_ISO`** (128 uses in `dashboard-routes`). Either export `NOW_ISO` from the fixture module and import it back, or pass it in. Either way it is computed once at module load, as now. `makeStores` brings `withFreshDigests`, and `makeRouter` brings the `withDefaults`-wrapped `createDashboardRoutes` and the three `InMemory*` stores. After the move, drop the now-unused `vm` and top-level `readFileSync` imports from `dashboard-routes` (the :4464 use imports its own).

**C. Piece 2 move: where the badge markup comes from, and one world per paint.**
- The real renderer is `renderRulingsBadge` in `lib/components/navbar.js:325`. It isn't exported. It reaches the page only through `renderNavBar(...)`, and only when `featureFlags.runControls === true` (:176). Render the navbar that way, or export the function, which is a small production change; say in the PR which you chose.
- On the real tree, `common.js:3152`'s selector `[data-rulings-badge][data-url-key="…"]` now has to match. The stub ignored the selector. That is a dead path coming alive, which is good.
- Build a fresh `loadWorld` for each `paint(urlKey)`, holding that workspace's badge, as one page has one badge. Supply the route's JSON with `globals: { fetch }`: `loadWorld`'s `globals` are copied over the default `fetch` stub.
- The test sits in `describe('LIN-4103 beat 3 — …')` (:6836). Keep that describe title in the new suite, or record the full path in the name map.

**D. The piece 2 rename mutation** (`workspaceCount` in the route) also turns the server-side test at :6850 red. That is expected, but say so in the PR, so the mutation result isn't read as an accident of the extraction.
